page: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-32GB is an x86_64 virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 4 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 200 GB SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 3844.87, placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-threaded gzip compression at 41.08 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 18.68 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing at 2862.0 also rank in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core and multi-threaded metrics fall into the average range, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6453.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 14373.65. Memory bandwidth is average, with large block read-only speeds at 103.01 GB/sec and write speeds at 47.08 GB/sec.

While single-core performance is strong, multi-core scaling is limited by the shared CPU allocation. LLM inference benchmarks demonstrate this tradeoff, where prompt processing for a small 135M model is average at 778.33 tokens/sec, but performance drops to a weak 23.71 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model. This resource profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high memory density without intensive multi-core demands. It is best suited for database operations, caching layers, text processing, and general-purpose web serving.
